thread:
alex: Quick sync — debt sprint kickoff. We need a lightweight 'stitch' playbook for temporary adapters when extracting enrichment service. Goal is minimal blast radius + easy rollback. Proposed pattern: sidecar adapter behind a feature flag, small contract shim lib, canary rollout + metrics, and a TTL cleanup ticket per adapter. Thoughts?
jia: +1 to the playbook idea. Can we make adapters strictly stateless so rollback is trivial? Also, prefer timeouts & circuit-breakers by default.
sasha: Agree. Add checklist: schema-compatibility, idempotency, backpressure handling, and clear error codes. Version adapters like `adapter.v1` so we can route explicitly.
michael: Question: fallback strategy — if adapter becomes flaky, what do we route to? My suggestion: route to legacy enrichment path with degraded QoS and increased sampling to verify parity.
alex: Yup — fallback policy = route -> legacy + sample to validate correctness. We'll treat parity checks as part of canary.
sasha: For the feature flag, propose a small CLI snippet for ops: 
```
# flip adapter on for 10% of traffic
./flagctl set enrichment-adapter --fraction=0.1 --tag=debt-sprint
```
Also, add span tag `enrichment.adapter=true` and metrics `enrichment.adapter.success_rate` / `enrichment.adapter.latency_ms`.
eng-bot: deploy started for `enrichment-adapter v0.1` to staging (ci-4567). See: https://ci/repo/4567
jia: Can we add a lightweight static lint that prevents calls to internal-only service endpoints from adapter code? Small safety net to avoid leaking internal APIs. I can prototype a check.
alex: Good idea — I'll own a lint ticket and add it to the debt-sprint board. Placeholder title: "adapter: ban internal-only endpoints via lint".
sasha: Cleanup governance: each adapter must create a TTL ticket (e.g., "remove/enrichment-adapter-post-extract") with a target date and owner; include a removal PR template. Also add a short rollout postmortem template that lists regressions and latency deltas.
michael: Ops runbook item: on >3m sustained 5xx or >50% error rate, auto-scale down adapter and flip feature flag off, route to legacy. We need a runbook owner. @sasha, can you pick this up?
sasha: I'll own the runbook. Will draft by EOD Wed and post in #eng-oncall.
alex: Action items recap: alex -> file lint ticket + link to repo; jia -> prototype static check + unit tests for idempotency; sasha -> runbook + removal PR template + canary metric dashboards; michael -> implement fallback routing policy prototype; eng-bot -> CI will publish staging artifact and smoke tests. Sync Thu 10:00am to validate smoke results. :rocket:
michael: One last thought — add a small feature in the router to do header-based routing so we can pin specific tenants to adapter traffic during canary. That will make debugging much easier.
alex: Agree — header pinning is low risk and high value. We'll add it as an optional router rule.
sasha: I'll include the router rule snippet in the runbook and a minimal integration test.
alex: Thanks everyone. Keeping the adapter surface tiny is our north star here. Short-lived tech debt is okay if we have concrete removal tickets and automation to delete. Meeting Thu 10am.
